places.name: Le Morne Brabant
places.blurb: A 556 m basalt monolith rising out of the south-west lagoon. The trail climbs through forest to a cross with one of the best views on the island.
places.fact: Maroons, people who escaped slavery, sheltered on its cliffs. The mountain has been a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape since 2008.
tips: Upper section: go with a guide
places.tags: hike mountain unesco sunrise history view climb

places.name: Île aux Cerfs
places.blurb: Powder-white beaches and a turquoise lagoon on an islet off the east coast. Come for the sandbanks, stay for the grilled fish.
places.fact: The islet even squeezes an 18-hole golf course in between its beaches.
places.tags: beach island catamaran swim snorkel boat lagoon

places.name: Chamarel Coloured Earth
places.blurb: Rolling dunes striped red, violet and ochre, five minutes from a waterfall that drops about 100 m into a forested gorge.
places.fact: The colours come from volcanic basalt weathered into clay. Mix the sands and they tend to settle back into separate layers.
tips: Waterfall viewpoint is on the same ticket
Say hi to the giant tortoises
places.tags: nature waterfall colours dunes rainy kids

places.name: Trou aux Cerfs
places.blurb: A dormant volcanic crater in the middle of Curepipe. Walk the rim road for a 360° view over the plateau and out to sea.
places.fact: Mauritius rose from the ocean floor as a hot-spot volcano about 8 million years ago.
tips: Cooler up here: bring a layer
Clear days show the whole west coast
places.tags: volcano crater view free rainy kids

places.name: Black River Gorges
places.blurb: The island’s largest national park: native forest, waterfalls and viewpoints over the gorges down to the west coast.
places.fact: It shelters the Mauritius kestrel, which recovered from just four known wild birds in 1974.
tips: Trail maps at Pétrin or the visitor centre
Hire a guide for Black River Peak
places.tags: hike forest birds nature waterfall trek

places.name: Grand Bassin
places.blurb: A sacred crater lake, Ganga Talao, ringed by Hindu temples, with monkeys on the steps and mist over the water.
places.fact: During Maha Shivaratri, hundreds of thousands of pilgrims walk here from all over the island.
places.tags: culture temple lake rainy history free sacred

places.name: Port Louis Market
places.blurb: The capital’s lively covered market: spice stalls, fruit pyramids, and the island’s favourite snack, dholl puri, a few steps away.
places.fact: Nearby Aapravasi Ghat (UNESCO) is the depot through which almost half a million indentured labourers arrived between 1834 and 1920.
places.tags: food market history unesco rainy city street dholl

places.name: Pamplemousses Garden
places.blurb: The Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam Botanical Garden: giant water lilies, spice trees and long avenues of palms.
places.fact: Its talipot palms flower only once, after decades, and then die.
tips: Hire a garden guide at the gate
L’Aventure du Sucre is next door
places.tags: nature garden kids rainy history lilies

places.name: Grand Baie
places.blurb: The north’s buzzing bay: catamarans by day, seafood, bars and live sega music by night.
places.fact: Boats leave from here for the northern islets such as Coin de Mire and Île Plate.
tips: La Cuvette is a quiet swim
Take a taxi back after dark
places.tags: food nightlife bar boat sunset beach seafood

places.name: Flic en Flac
places.blurb: One of the longest beaches on the island, lined with filao trees and food vans, facing the sunset.
places.fact: The west coast is sheltered from the trade winds, so its lagoon is usually calmest in winter.
tips: Food vans by the public beach
Snorkel the reef at the south end

places.name: Tamarin Bay dolphins
places.blurb: Spinner and bottlenose dolphins rest in the bay in the early morning. Watch from a boat that keeps its distance.
places.fact: Mauritius has dolphin- and whale-watching regulations: boats must keep their distance and limit time near a pod.
tips: Pick operators that follow the code
Never chase or swim at them
places.tags: dolphin whale boat morning kids sea

places.name: Blue Bay Marine Park
places.blurb: A protected lagoon of coral gardens near Mahébourg, made for snorkelling and glass-bottom boats.
places.fact: The park is a Ramsar wetland of international importance, listed in 2008.
places.tags: beach snorkel coral kids boat swim lagoon

places.name: Gris Gris
places.blurb: Wild southern cliffs with no reef offshore: Indian Ocean rollers smash straight into the black rocks.
places.fact: Nearby La Roche qui Pleure, “the crying rock”, seems to weep as the waves drain off it.
places.tags: nature cliffs view free waves wild

places.name: Belle Mare
places.blurb: A long white east-coast beach with a wide, shallow lagoon for sunrise swims and kayaks.
places.fact: The east coast faces the trade winds, so it gets breezy from June to September.
tips: Swim early, wind picks up after noon

places.name: Île aux Aigrettes
places.blurb: A tiny islet reserve where coastal ebony forest is being restored and giant tortoises roam free.
places.fact: It is run by the Mauritian Wildlife Foundation, and tour fees help fund its conservation work.

places.name: Casela Nature Park
places.blurb: Ziplines over the canyon, quad safaris and an animal park on the slopes above the west coast.
places.fact: From the upper lines you can see across Tamarin Bay to Le Morne.

places.name: Mahébourg
places.blurb: A laid-back fishing town on Grand Port bay with a big Monday market, hot gâteaux piments and a waterfront promenade.
places.fact: The 1810 Battle of Grand Port, fought in this bay, is the only French naval victory engraved on the Arc de Triomphe.
tips: Monday market is the big one

places.name: Cap Malheureux
places.blurb: The red-roofed chapel at the island’s northern tip, looking out to the wedge of Coin de Mire.
places.fact: Its name means “Cape of Misfortune”, after the ships wrecked on the reefs offshore.
places.tags: culture church view photo free sunset

places.name: Tamarind Falls
places.blurb: Seven waterfalls stepping down a basalt canyon: hike, swim in plunge pools or abseil with a guide.
places.fact: The falls drain the wet central plateau and run highest after the summer rains.
